comparisons.peer_topic: Capital and RWA Changes at Year-End 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: At December 31, 2024, CET1 capital increased to $201.1 billion, Tier 1 capital rose $135 million, and Total capital under Standardized approach increased $4.0 billion, while RWA grew $44.5 billion to $1,696 billion driven by client and lending activity.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America disclose Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA) calculated under the Standardized Approach for their 2024 fiscal year. JPMorgan highlights a specific $43.3 billion portion of Credit risk RWA attributed to First Republic assets under transition provisions, whereas Bank of America reports a total Standardized RWA of $1,696 billion driven by broader client and lending activity, without isolating a merger-related transition portfolio in this specific data point.

sentences.text: (d)As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, Credit risk RWA reflected approximately $43.3 billion and $52.4 billion, respectively, of RWA calculated under the Standardized approach for certain assets associated with First Republic as permitted by the transition provisions in the U.S. capital rules.

RWA under the Standardized approach, which yielded the lower CET1 capital ratio at December 31, 2024, increased $44.5 billion during 2024 to $1,696 billion primarily driven by client activity in Global Markets and lending activity in GWIM, Global Banking and Consumer Banking.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citigroup's CET1 Capital ratio increased to 13.6% as of December 31, 2024, from 13.4% in 2023, driven by net income and a decrease in risk-weighted assets, partially offset by dividends, share repurchases, and AOCI movements.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Citigroup report regulatory capital metrics based on the Basel III Standardized Approach. JPMorgan details specific RWA amounts for First Republic assets under transition provisions within its Credit risk RWA, while Citigroup reports its overall CET1 Capital ratio (13.6%) determined using the Standardized Approach, driven by net income and RWA changes.

sentences.text: (d)As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, Credit risk RWA reflected approximately $43.3 billion and $52.4 billion, respectively, of RWA calculated under the Standardized approach for certain assets associated with First Republic as permitted by the transition provisions in the U.S. capital rules.
Citigroup's CET1 Capital ratio was 13.6% as of December 31, 2024, compared to 13.4% as of December 31, 2023, based on the Basel III Standardized Approach for determining risk weighted assets (RWA).

comparisons.peer_topic: Capital Return and Regulatory Capital Ratios
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm returned $11.80 billion to shareholders via repurchases and dividends in 2024, while maintaining strong regulatory capital positions with a CET1 ratio of 15.0% under Standardized Rules and 15.3% under Advanced Rules as of December 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs disclose capital position metrics calculated under the Standardized Capital Rules. JPMorgan specifies RWA amounts for First Republic assets under Standardized transition provisions, while Goldman Sachs reports its CET1 capital ratio of 15.0% under the Standardized Capital Rules, indicating compliance with the same regulatory framework.

sentences.text: (d)As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, Credit risk RWA reflected approximately $43.3 billion and $52.4 billion, respectively, of RWA calculated under the Standardized approach for certain assets associated with First Republic as permitted by the transition provisions in the U.S. capital rules.
As of December 2024, our CET1 capital ratio was 15.0% under the Standardized Capital Rules and 15.3% under the Advanced Capital Rules.

comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, Credit risk RWA increased under both the Standardized and Advanced Approaches, primarily due to growth in Corporate lending and Securities financing transactions, partially offset by decreased exposure in derivatives or investment securities.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley discuss Credit risk RWA changes under the Standardized Approach. JPMorgan quantifies the static RWA stock for First Republic assets ($43.3 billion) under transition provisions, while Morgan Stanley explains the drivers of Credit risk RWA increases under the Standardized Approach during 2024, citing growth in Corporate lending and Securities financing transactions.

sentences.text: (d)As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, Credit risk RWA reflected approximately $43.3 billion and $52.4 billion, respectively, of RWA calculated under the Standardized approach for certain assets associated with First Republic as permitted by the transition provisions in the U.S. capital rules.
In 2024, Credit risk RWA increased under both the Standardized and Advanced Approaches.

Under the Standardized Approach, the increase was primarily due to higher Securities financing transactions, growth in Corporate lending, as well as an increase in Other credit risk driven by securitizations.
